Subject: Request: short-term GPU carve for Zephyr pilot

Hi Tessa —

Hope you’re well. We’re ramping the Zephyr AI enterprise pilot the week of Nov 23 for three core workloads (inference, embeddings, and nightly reranks). Our ops team is concerned about cold-start autoscale during the first 72 hours — we’d like to request a short-term static carve (8 A100 slots) for the pilot week to guarantee latency SLAs.

Attached is our pilot traffic forecast and token-level estimate. We understand this is an exception to standard autoscale behavior and are happy to cover reservation fees.

Key asks:
- Temporary carve: Nov 22 00:00 UTC -> Nov 29 23:59 UTC
- 8 A100-equivalent slots (burst-capable)
- Commitment to alert and revert if utilization < 30% for >24h

Can you confirm feasibility and what approval path is needed? We’ll loop procurement if necessary: procurement@zephyrai.com.

Thanks — Sasha
Sasha Korolev
Head of Cloud Operations, Zephyr AI

Internal owners, can infra confirm whether a Nov 22 start is operationally feasible and what controls we need to put in place? I’ve attached the forecast to the thread for reference.

Next steps I propose: internal feasibility + draft reservation terms by Mon Nov 15, then sync with Zephyr for signatures.

Subject: Re: Request: short-term GPU carve for Zephyr pilot

Tessa / team —

We evaluated the ask against current pool utilization and autoscale config. Short summary:

- Feasible as a time-bound exception using a "burst window" policy that pins capacity for up to 7 days. Implementation steps: create a temporary reservation resource (res-ztp-2026-11-22) linked to Zephyr account, set max_preemptions=1, eviction_policy=notify, and scoped to the west-us pool.
- Risk: ~5% chance of latency regressions for other high-priority legacy tenants if a region-level incident occurs during the window. We can mitigate by adding a fallback policy to route to compatible model variants (smaller size) and reduce burst to 6 slots automatically if region-wide contention > 70%.
- Ops automation: requires a short runbook update and a temporary webhook that notifies Zephyr and our oncall on every preemption event. See draft runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-zephyr-pilot (autoscale_burst_runbook_v2.md attached).

I recommend the following guardrails before we approve:
1) signed reservation agreement and deal id assigned (sales).
2) limit to 7 days with a hard cutover and automatic scale-down policy at the 48-hour mark if avgutil < 30%.
3) oncall alerting configured and a primary/secondary pager assigned.

If sales confirms payment/commit, infra can schedule the reservation change on Nov 21 (UTC) to avoid disruption.

- Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: autoscale_burst_runbook_v2.md (runbook draft)
